name: DocVQA
description: DocVQA is a large scale dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Questions are categorized based on reasoning requirements (9 question types: handwritten, form, layout, table/list, other, running text, photograph, figure, yes/no). The dataset is split 80-10-10 into train (39,463 questions, 10,194 images), validation (5,349 questions, 1,286 images), and test (5,188 questions, 1,287 images) sets.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar (CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India; Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain)
citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV], 5 Jan 2021.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Pages were hand-picked from documents across different collections and industries. Binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality as a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. Questions and answers were collected using remote workers via a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/), spanning documents from 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical), drawn from 6,071 industry documents ranging from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018; most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: OCR tokens from document images were serialized to a single string separated by space in top-left to bottom-right order. For BERT QA models, data was prepared in SQuAD style format where answers are defined as spans with start and end indices, using the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string (following TriviaQA approach).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized. Pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures were prioritized. OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application. Data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation, and test splits. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were excluded from the dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages using a web-based annotation tool with remote workers. Stage 1: Workers were shown a document image and asked to define up to 10 question-answer pairs, entering answers verbatim from the document. Multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged where warranted. Stage 2: A different worker was shown the image and questions (without stage 1 answers), required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. Stage 3: If no answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers or add new answers before accepting or ignoring the question.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in stage 1 matched exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for third-stage review by the authors. Questions flagged as inapt (due to language issues or ambiguity) in stage 2 were not included in the dataset. Multiple ground truth answers per question were allowed.
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 annotators per question (stage 1 and stage 2 workers), with author review for mismatched cases in stage 3. Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application (used to extract OCR tokens from document images for statistics and baseline experiments)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code, and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains industry documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library that may include names of people, institutions, and places as answers. Named entities such as names of people appear among the most common non-numeric answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research, enabling intelligent reading systems to respond to ad-hoc information requests expressed in natural language. This could drive methods that use low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: A large majority of questions start with 'what is the', asking for date, title, total, amount, or name. Most top answers are numeric values due to a high number of report and invoice images. Many documents are from food and nutrition related collections as they have a good number of non-binarized images, which may skew industry representation.
rai:dataLimitations: Existing models perform significantly below human performance (94.36% accuracy), especially on questions requiring understanding of document structure. Models need improvement on questions involving figures, text on photographs, and handwriting. OCR errors can result in incorrect answers even when models correctly ground questions. The copy mechanism in some models cannot output answers combining two or more OCR tokens.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on document images. The dataset is intended for extractive QA where answers are spans of text present in the document image. It can also be used for benchmarking reading comprehension models adapted for document images. A leaderboard is available at docvqa.org.
